valores.descripcion: We promote empathy, human quality, and respect in all our actions, fostering a fairer and more supportive society.
We guarantee equal treatment for all people, without discrimination based on gender, age, origin, or social condition, ensuring democratic access to culture and art.
We believe in art as a fundamental means for individual and collective expression, encouraging the development of critical thinking and innovation.
We use art as a tool for social transformation, promoting peaceful coexistence and violence prevention.
We recognize the impact of art on emotional stability, providing spaces that favor psychological balance and overall well-being.
We build bonds of unity through artistic and cultural activities that strengthen family and social ties.
We value and promote the richness of different cultural expressions, encouraging the recognition and appreciation of collective identity.
We seek to balance information overload with meaningful cultural education that supports the integral development of society.
We defend everyone's right to access culture, eliminating economic and social barriers that limit participation.

preguntas.respuesta: The Complejo Integral de Cultura (CIC) is a non-profit organization and an authorized charity, which allows us to offer quality cultural services at affordable costs thanks to donations. We are a cutting-edge cultural space in Tapachula that promotes training, research, promotion, and dissemination of the arts. Through workshops, activities, and artistic programs, we contribute to the development of inclusive, sensitive, and participatory audiences, reaffirming our commitment to democratic access to culture.
We offer workshops in music, dance, theater, and visual arts, as well as events such as festivals, exhibitions, artistic performances, and social inclusion programs.
For children, youth, and adults of all ages, with or without prior experience. CIC is an open space for the entire community.
We promote art as a tool for peace, mental health, and social cohesion, creating safe spaces for free expression and community strengthening.

preguntas.pregunta: Does CIC offer support or scholarships?
preguntas.respuesta: Yes. We have the "BecArte & Más" program, which supports students and emerging artists with limited resources. Additionally, the prices of our workshops include a scholarship from the organization, making them affordable for the community.

preguntas.pregunta: How can I participate in CIC's activities?
preguntas.respuesta: You can register for workshops on our website, attend cultural events, join community projects, and apply for our scholarships and volunteer programs.
In Tapachula, Chiapas, serving as a cultural reference in southern Mexico.

transparencia.info:
At the Integral Center for Culture (CIC), we embrace transparency and accountability as pillars of our mission: to educate, create, research, teach, and promote the arts with ethical, social, and humanist values.

To date, we have not received support from foundations or public funds; our projects have been financed exclusively through local collaborations and sponsorships from individuals and businesses committed to culture in Tapachula, Chiapas. This path has required careful, responsible, and verifiable management, which we now make available to anyone wishing to contribute, either financially or in-kind.

Open invitation: We invite you to explore our workshops, rehearsals, and productions. Culture grows with trust: your donation becomes living art and real opportunities for our community.

secciones.respuesta:
• Solid operational history: we conduct permanent workshops, festivals, exhibitions, and recitals meeting objectives, schedules, and budgets. In projects with partners, the budget contributed by each collaborator is labeled and managed by them, with approval and verification per project.
  • Governance and internal controls: we maintain strict separation of duties to authorize, execute, and verify expenses. For each event, an operational committee of volunteers (art students) assumes defined roles and applies documentary verification and inventory safeguarding through logs and handover records.
  • Proactive transparency: together with involved students, we compile project folders with budget, execution, and report; income/expense summaries; logs of in-kind donations; and scholarship allocation criteria. All information is presented and made available to the community within 30 days after each event.
  • Integrity and conflict of interest: zero-tolerance policy on corruption and guidelines to prevent and declare potential conflicts of interest.
  • Access and verification: open doors for visits and social audit; we provide evidence (photos, videos, handover records, attendance lists, contracts, and invoices when applicable).

1. Artistic programming: production of festivals, exhibitions, recitals, and training residencies (rooms, technical support, logistics, promotion, insurance, documentation).
  2. BecArte & Más scholarships: support for children, adolescents, and adults in vulnerable situations for registration, tuition, materials, and pedagogical guidance.
  3. Equipment and maintenance: instruments, costumes, lighting, audio, scenography, furniture, digital infrastructure, and accessibility.
  4. Teacher training and professionalization: updates, certifications, and teaching materials.
Priority principle: we prioritize spending directly on programs and impact, minimizing administrative costs and publishing cost structure per project.

• Cash donation: bank transfer, deposit, or sponsorship agreement (labeled per project if requested).
  • In-kind donation: musical instruments, technical equipment, costumes, materials, printing, transport, lodging, food, spaces, professional services.
  • Corporate and pro bono volunteering: legal/accounting advice, design, communication, production, health and wellness for cast and students.
  • Strategic partnerships: co-production of events, named scholarships, sponsorships with visibility and impact metrics.
If your organization requires specific formats (e.g., ESG/SDG metrics or traceable reports), we design and report them compatible with your internal policies.

In this section, we make available —for consultation and download— the following resources (as applicable and current):
  • Institutional framework: bylaws, statutes, corporate purpose, tax ID, and local/state records.
  • Planning and results: annual work program, indicators, quarterly reports, and annual review.
  • Finance and control: project budgets, summarized income/expense statements, in-kind donation logs, inventories, and handover records.
  • Institutional policies: integrity, procurement, donations, child protection, equality and non-discrimination, privacy, and image use.
  • BecArte & Más scholarships: call for applications, selection criteria, scholarship committee, number of beneficiaries (aggregated and anonymized data), and academic follow-up.
Updates are published quarterly. Each project is identified by name, date, location, and responsible person, with its consultation folder.
